entrada.titulo: Enhancing anomaly detection and prevention in Internet of Things (IoT) using deep neural networks and blockchain based cyber security

perfil_anterior.solucao: hybrid DNN-Blockchain architecture for IoT network security
perfil_anterior.limites: computational cost analysis for DNN training and blockchain operations is necessary

hidden layers. Advanced Activation Functions for increased non-linearity, dropout layers to reduce overfitting, 
and batch normalization for stable learning to improve model performance are among the methods used in 
regularisation & optimization layers. The output layer generates a categorization label or anomaly score, 
providing interesting analysis. The DNNs-BCT framework’s feature selection procedure aims to improve 
anomaly detection accuracy with little computational cost. The model leverages key characteristics collected 
from blockchain security events, device activity logs, and network traffic to zero in on the most important cyber 
danger indicators. Data exfiltration and distributed denial of service attacks can be detected using traffic-based 
features such as packet size distribution, flow duration, and protocol usage. Irregular communication patterns 
can be identified using statistical features such as network flows’ mean, variance, and entropy. Behavioral features, 
such as failed authentication attempts, access pattern deviations, and anomalies in smart contract invocation, 
can be used to uncover Sybil and brute-force attacks, which are blockchain-based threats. To train DNNs with 
the most relevant network behaviors, the feature set is refined using methods like Recursive Feature Elimination 
(RFE), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Mutual Information-Based Selection.Most importantly, for 
applications such as anomaly detection, classification, and more, this ordered DL pipeline ensures efficient data 
processing, enabling models to grasp complex patterns and produce accurate predictions.

Figure 4 shows an IoT network traffic anomaly detection system based on DNN. It consists mostly of two 
main processes: data collecting and preprocessing and anomaly detection. The first stage intercepts network 
traffic and generates features. Data forms a dataset employing preprocessing and labeling. The next division of 
the dataset is 25% for testing and 75% for training. During the second step, a DNN learns to spot anomalies in 
the dataset. The trained model sets network behavior as either normal, benign, or aberrant, either benign or 
dangerous. An alert indicates a likely security risk upon an anomaly discovered. This technology guarantees IoT 
network integrity by employing machine learning techniques to spot suspicious activity in real-time, improving 
IoT security and helping to lower cyber risks.
